transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alex (CTO, Verdant), Priya (Head of Security), Tom (DevOps), Hannah (PM)
---
Summary: quick runthrough of pilot telemetry results, focused conformance items: SSO/SAML end-to-end, audit logs schema and retention behavior, SOC2 evidence ask and private deployment readiness. Agreed next steps and owners.
Topics: SSO test failures, audit log format and redaction, retention lifecycles, SOC2 attestation evidence, dedicated capacity pricing, staging access for E2E tests.
Action items (recap): see action_items metadata above.

Transcript body:
[00:00:05] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining i think we have about 45 minutes so we can go through the telemetry quickly then dive into the sso and logs. Maya and I will drive.
[00:00:18] Alex: great thanks. quick note we ran the 48 hour smoke yesterday, saw a couple of auth timeouts and a weird token mismatch on the third replay.
[00:00:30] Maya: ok can you describe the token mismatch, alex? was that on initial handshake or on the refresh?
[00:00:38] Alex: it looked like the session cookie expired but the id token still valid, so our client tried to refresh and the runtime returned a 401, i pasted the trace in the ticket.
[00:00:48] Tom: yeah i added logs, looks like our saml response had an unexpected NameID format for one test user. probably a mapping issue from our idp.
[00:00:58] Maya: that fits what we saw — Redwood's gateway validates SAML assertions and then issues internal session tokens. if the NameID doesn't match mapping we can reject, which shows up as a 401. we can relax mapping rules for the pilot if you want but for prod we'd want strict mapping.
[00:01:14] Priya: for compliance we need to understand what assertions are retained, how long, and whether they're reversible back to PII. we have strict rules: raw SAML assertions must be retained for 90 days for investigation but PII fields must be redacted in long-term logs.
[00:01:31] Maya: understood. we have two tiers of logs: short-term complete audit events (kept 90 days by default) and long-term aggregated traces with PII redacted. we can also plug in your KMS and manage envelope encryption.
[00:01:46] Jordan: quick note on SOC2 — customers often want the Type II report; we'll share our latest attestation and the list of control owners.
[00:01:55] Priya: yes please, also we need to map controls to evidence. e.g. audit log configuration, SSO SAML flows, key management for encryption.
[00:02:06] Jordan: we'll send that.
[00:02:10] Hannah: from product side i'm mostly tracking retention and data classification — can we get a sample audit export so i can show legal?
[00:02:18] Maya: absolutely — i'll produce a sanitized example that mirrors real fields: timestamp, event_type, resource_id, session_id, user_hash, action, outcome, metadata. we'll redact or hash emails.
[00:02:32] Alex: perfect. for the pilot we have three classes: session traces (90 days), request/response payloads (7 days unless sensitive), and aggregated metrics (3 years). will that align?
[00:02:44] Maya: we can do that per-route. the runtime supports route-level retention policies and on-demand purge API. note: payloads that are marked sensitive trigger additional retention rules and optional customer-managed encryption.
[00:02:58] Tom: how does purge work for cached kv entries, we use prefix caching for repeated prompts — need to ensure purge clears KV and prefix caches as well.
[00:03:08] Maya: good question. purge will invalidate KV cache entries and also clear prefix cache for matching keys; we will include the sample API call in the audit export doc.
[00:03:18] Alex: what's the expected RTO if we run a customer-initiated purge?
[00:03:23] Maya: typically under 2 minutes for small keyspaces; for large-scale purges it can take longer, but we can provide a job status endpoint so you can track progress.
[00:03:33] Priya: another ask — do you support SSO session lifetime enforcement from IdP? we want idle timeout of 15 minutes and absolute timeout of 8 hours.
[00:03:44] Maya: yes, we honor IdP session assertions and can also enforce additional server-side timeouts. for the pilot we can configure idle=15m and absolute=8h.
[00:03:53] Jordan: switching to evidence: we'll attach our SOC2 Type II PDF and a mapping spreadsheet. two caveats: some vendor-specific controls are covered by subprocessors, we'll annotate those.
[00:04:06] Priya: ok, good. on encryption — is customer-managed KMS supported for both hosted and private deployments?
[00:04:13] Maya: yes. hosted can integrate with your cloud KMS (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) via envelope encryption. private deployment can use your HSM or on-prem KMS.
[00:04:24] Tom: for the dedicated nodes we talked about, are audit logs streamed to our S3 bucket or do we pull them?
[00:04:31] Maya: both options exist. we can stream real-time to your S3 with SSE-KMS and provide batched deliveries. we'll include example S3 lifecycle rules.
[00:04:41] Hannah: what about search — will legal be able to query logs? we don't want raw PII searchable after 7 days.
[00:04:48] Maya: search indices only include hashed user identifiers after the retention window; raw PII is removed per the retention policy.
[00:04:55] Alex: i want to call out an intermittent 5xx rate we saw during heavy replay. not security but impacts compliance baseline for availability.
[00:05:05] Jordan: we saw that in telemetry — it correlates with a quantization path on a long sequence. Maya, did we patch the kernel?
[00:05:12] Maya: yes we deployed a fix to how the runtime handles padding and long kv cache windows, reduced 5xx from 2.3% to 0.4 in internal tests. we'll push the same build to your pilot cluster tonight.
[00:05:24] Tom: can we get a canary first? we prefer a single instance rollout in staging.
[00:05:28] Maya: absolutely, we'll canary to one zone and monitor errors and latency for 6 hours before full rollout.
[00:05:36] Priya: loop back to audit log content: we need assurance that logs cannot be retroactively altered — tamper evidence.
[00:05:43] Maya: our audit pipeline supports append-only storage with SHA256 chain hashes and proof-of-write to S3; for private deployments you can bring an integrity monitor. we'll include architecture diagram.
[00:05:55] Alex: sounds good. one more item: we might require a short-term retention exception for a legal hold — can that be applied per-customer and tracked?
[00:06:05] Jordan: yes we support legal hold flags that temporarily extend retention; we'll log the action and require an authorized approver.
[00:06:12] Hannah: for timeline — pilot ends mid-May, we need final compliance signoff end of May. are we on track?
[00:06:20] Jordan: if staging SSO tests and audit examples land this week and we run a 24h replay next week, should be in good shape.
[00:06:26] Maya: i'll produce the audit export and the purge API examples today/tomorrow.
[00:06:31] Tom: i will share IdP metadata by Thursday.
[00:06:35] Priya: i'll assemble the retention windows doc and control-owner list.
[00:06:40] Jordan: great. moving on briefly to dedicated-capacity pricing — i have three tiers for pilot: shared-hosted (baseline), reserved 2x GPUs, reserved 4x GPUs with SLA. will email numbers after this call.
[00:06:53] Alex: for our use we likely need reserved 2x GPUs for predictable latency; please include burst options.
[00:06:59] Jordan: yes we'll include burst policy and estimated token costs with the quote.
[00:07:04] Maya: ops note: when you run the SSO E2E test please include at least one user with multi-tenant group membership to exercise group mappings. we saw mapping edge cases there.
[00:07:15] Tom: will do.
[00:07:18] Jordan: any blockers left?
[00:07:20] Priya: just need the SOC2 docs and audit log example. otherwise ok.
[00:07:24] Jordan: ok we'll send those post-call.
[00:07:27] Hannah: one ask — can you include an example incident response play for leaked tokens? our infosec team wants to see the steps.
[00:07:34] Maya: yes we'll add an incident response playbook extract showing detection, containment, revocation, notification, and evidence collection steps.
[00:07:44] Alex: great.
[00:07:46] Jordan: recap of next steps then: maya will share sanitized audit export + purge API + incident playbook; jordan will share SOC2 attestation + dedicated pricing; tom will hand over IdP metadata; priya will provide retention windows. we'll target the staging E2E SSO test on Friday.
[00:07:59] Priya: confirmed.
[00:08:02] Jordan: thanks everyone. we can close unless anyone has anything else — quick check?
[00:08:08] Tom: none here.
[00:08:10] Alex: no thanks, good meeting.
[00:08:12] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and schedule. bye.
[00:08:18] [call ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap and some product names transcribed as generic terms (e.g., 'kv cache' as 'k v cache'), punctuation and proper nouns may be imperfect. The transcript includes natural hesitations and filler words (um, uh) which were lightly cleaned for readability.
